title: fndn/ui component spec
description: Framework-agnostic description of one component: its anatomy (parts), props, states, tokens, and dependencies. The recipe and every adapter (React, Vue, Svelte) must implement exactly this.

name.description: kebab-case id: the name of the component's folder and files, of its data-slot, and of the component in the tool

title.description: Title Case, as shown in the docs ("Button Group", "Date Picker")

summary.description: One plain sentence for people: what it is or what it is for. No px, tokens, engine or helper names; the docs show it at the top of the page and llms.txt lists it.

description.description: The full description: how it looks and behaves, the details the summary leaves out.

kind.description: component = a basic building block (button, select, dialog); block = built from several components for a product use (approval card, records table)

marked.description: false: the adapters build this part through a helper, so a literal data-slot is not in their source (say why in description). Final shape only.

attr.description: how the prop reaches CSS: a data-* / aria-* attribute, a CSS custom property (--fndn-*), or a native attribute

part.description: anatomy part the attr lands on (default: root)

ts.description: The prop's TypeScript type when `type` cannot say it (a union such as HTMLElement | string | (() => HTMLElement | null)). The generated docs show it instead of `type`.

files.description: For a component whose adapter is several files in a framework: their names, per framework, in the component's folder. Left out, the adapter is <name>.tsx (React), <PascalName>.vue, <PascalName>.svelte.

category.description: Where the component sits in the catalogue and the docs tree.

order.description: Sort order inside its category (ascending; ties by name).

engine.description: Zag.js machine behind the component, when it has one (for example 'select'). Adapters then use the matching Ark UI component.

targets.description: The frameworks this component has an adapter for. Left out: all three. A new component may list only "react" until its Vue and Svelte adapters exist.
